analyst_note: Hormuz Day 111 — Deal T-1: Lebanon Quiet Day 3 CLEARED — All Three Pre-Signing Performance Tests Passed; Geneva Signing June 19 T-0 Tomorrow — Vance, Witkoff, Kushner Confirmed; Naval Blockade Dissolution Day 4; CENTCOM Stand-Down Day 4 — Shipping Companies Hold Wait-and-See Pending Formal Signing; WTI ~$75 — Fifth Consecutive Decline — Full Deal-Completion Pricing; Iran Comms Resolved Day 17; WPA Day 110 — Day 20 Past Hard Constitutional Deadline — Deal Moot Pathway Active; Acting DNI Day 28; CISA Day 48 Clean; Shamkhani Cyber Day 25; Secure America Act Law Day 5; Reconciliation 2.0 16 Days to July 4 — No Floor Date — FC Leverage Dissolving Day 4; Oklahoma Senate Primary: Kevin Hern Wins; Georgia Runoffs: Collins Advances Senate; Jackson Defeats Trump-Backed Jones for Governor; JD Vance CoS Nick Luna Day 2; CRITICAL PNW: Upriver Fire (Spokane NE, WUI Day 2, ~350+ Acres, 11,000+ Evacuations, 15+ Homes Destroyed, 1 Missing — First WUI Structure-Loss Event of 2026 PNW Season; Governor Ferguson FEMA Declaration Requested); Juniper Dunes CONTAINMENT BREAKTHROUGH — 13,144 Acres 20% (Up From 0% June 17); Twin Sisters CONTAINMENT BREAKTHROUGH — 8,262 Acres 65% (Up From 0% June 17); Lake Sutherland (Olympic Peninsula, Day 2, Status Uncertain); CONFIRMED HEAT DEATHS: Multnomah County 4 Suspected Heat Fatalities From June 14-16 Event; Washington Heat Mortality Monitoring Continues; NIFC Above-Normal Day 18; NIFC-FIFA Co-Response Day 11; Seattle FIFA T-1 — US vs Australia TOMORROW June 19 Pride Weekend Lumen Field; Washington Drought Day 14 (4th Year); Oregon 83% Drought; NSF Newport OR ~10 Days; BPA Grid Stabilizing. Thursday June 18, 2026 evening. The June 18 evening brief closes at Vibe 6 — the first upgrade since the June 14 deal declaration elevated the score from 4 upper-edge to 5. The upgrade is granted tonight on Lebanon Quiet Day 3 confirmed: all three consecutive pre-signing performance tests have been passed. No Israeli military action in Lebanon materialized in the June 18 cycle. No Iranian kinetic response was executed. Hezbollah has conducted no additional northern Israel operations since June 15. With Lebanon Day 1 (June 16), Day 2 (June 17), and Day 3 (June 18) all clear — and the Geneva formal signing ceremony now hours away — the primary deal-collapse scenario is operationally exhausted. The session's second defining development is the sharpest single-day PNW fire bifurcation of the 2026 season: the June 17-18 cooling window produced dramatic simultaneous containment breakthroughs on both Juniper Dunes (0% → 20%, 13,144 acres) and Twin Sisters (0% → 65%, 8,262 acres) — the first positive operational fire signal of the year — but was simultaneously punctuated by the season's first wildland-urban interface structure-loss event. The Upriver Fire ignited northeast of Spokane on June 17, wind-driven into a densely populated Spokane County neighborhood, forcing 11,000+ people under evacuation orders, threatening 500+ homes, destroying at least 15 structures, and leaving one person reported missing. Governor Bob Ferguson has requested a FEMA fire management assistance declaration — the first state-requested federal fire emergency of the 2026 season — marking the Upriver Fire as the most consequential wildfire event of the arc to date by human impact metrics. The humanitarian cost of the June 14-16 heat wave also now has a documented death toll: Multnomah County is investigating 4 suspected heat-related fatalities, all confirmed in the June 17-18 lag window identified in prior briefs. From a political economy standpoint, June 18 delivers a noteworthy primary data point: Trump-backed Georgia gubernatorial candidate Lt. Gov. Burt Jones lost the GOP runoff to Rick Jackson, the first Trump-endorsed statewide candidate loss in the post-deal primary cycle. Oklahoma's Kevin Hern won the Senate primary. The dual result — Trump's Senate pick winning, gubernatorial pick losing — introduces the first evidence of primary-environment differentiation in the post-deal political landscape.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 6 — upgraded from Vibe 5 (June 16-17 level); three conditions from the Vibe 6 upgrade checklist now satisfied, with the fourth (formal Geneva signing) executing tomorrow T-0. Lebanon Quiet Day 3 cleared: all three pre-signing performance tests passed, the explicit prerequisite identified in the June 15 deal declaration arc. The deal-collapse scenario — Israeli Lebanon strike triggering Iranian response before Geneva — has not materialized across any of the three required pre-signing days; Netanyahu restraint through the full window is now confirmed. WTI at approximately $75 on the fifth consecutive decline day confirms markets have fully priced deal completion and sanctions-lifting; the oil price signal is the strongest external validator of deal stability available. Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters containment breakthroughs (20% and 65% respectively) represent the first genuine operational fire success of the 2026 PNW season and reduce the peak fire threat load materially. Three factors prevent a higher score tonight: formal Geneva signing has not yet occurred (T-0 tomorrow — the deal's full legal architecture does not activate until signing); the Upriver Fire represents a genuine WUI humanitarian crisis with ongoing evacuations, structure loss, and one missing person — the first confirmed wildfire structural-loss event of the season; and Multnomah County's 4 confirmed suspected heat fatalities mark the week's human cost as documented, not projected. Upgrade to 7 requires: June 19 formal signing confirmed + Hormuz physical reopening to unescorted commercial transits announced + no overnight deal-disrupting event. Drop to 5 requires: Iranian MOU repudiation or Israeli Lebanon strike tonight triggering Iranian response; Upriver Fire escalation into mass-casualty or critical infrastructure event.

items.summary: The June 18 geopolitical session delivers the single signal the 111-day arc has been building toward: Lebanon Quiet Day 3 cleared. No confirmed new Israeli military action in Lebanon materialized in the June 18 cycle. Hezbollah conducted no additional northern Israel drone attacks. Iran did not execute its threatened kinetic response. Trump's June 14 'don't blow it' warning to Netanyahu held across all three pre-signing performance days. The primary deal-collapse scenario — Israeli Lebanon operations triggering Iranian response before Geneva — has been extinguished across the full pre-signing window. The June 19 formal signing ceremony in Geneva is T-0. Vice President JD Vance, Middle East special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner are confirmed attending the ceremony. The MOU calls for Hormuz to reopen immediately without tolls, Iran to receive sanctions relief tied to compliance, the ceasefire to extend 60 days including Lebanon, and nuclear negotiations to commence within the 60-day window. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif confirmed the June 19 signing date as mediator. The MOU was electronically endorsed by Trump, Vance, and Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf ahead of the formal ceremony. CENTCOM continues blockade dissolution Day 4: the US Navy has established 'safe pathways for commercial vessels' through Hormuz, and CENTCOM has confirmed hundreds of ships have transited under escort in the past months. However, three days into the deal declaration, commercial marine traffic has not yet meaningfully resumed at pre-closure levels. Shipping companies and insurance underwriters are maintaining a wait-and-see posture, holding off on unescorted transits until the June 19 formal signing triggers the MOU's legal architecture. Ship tracking data confirms the resumption lag. The formal signing tomorrow is the expected trigger for shipping companies to reroute and for insurance market rates to begin normalizing. Until that happens, Hormuz is nominally open but commercially inert.

items.summary: Oil markets on June 18 are pricing a fully resolved Hormuz arc: WTI has declined for the fifth consecutive session, approaching approximately $75 per barrel on the Thursday close, tracking toward the $74-78 post-signing range as deal mechanics and Iranian production re-entry begin to be modeled. The decline began at $81 on the June 15 Monday open immediately following Trump's June 14 deal declaration and has continued without interruption. The WTI trajectory is the clearest market signal available that the deal probability is being priced as near-certain ahead of the June 19 formal signing. Brent tracking to approximately $80. However, the full market impact of deal completion is partially front-running the actual supply-side trigger: shipping companies and insurance underwriters are maintaining a wait-and-see posture pending the June 19 formal signing. The 100+ oil-laden ships currently stuck in or near the Gulf have not yet moved; marine traffic has not resumed at pre-closure levels despite CENTCOM's safe pathway announcements. The June 19 signing is the expected commercial trigger — at signing, the sanctions waiver activates, tanker operators begin repositioning, and insurance rates begin normalizing. The supply increase from Iran's production re-entry will take 4-6 weeks to fully materialize at the pump; US gasoline price relief (Oregon $5.35, national $4.564) is 2-4 weeks post-signing. The June FOMC dot plot and Warsh's June 17 inaugural press conference are now processing in the rearview mirror — the at-least-three 2026 hike projections were absorbed without market dislocation as pre-deal artifacts. The September FOMC (next SEP) is the operative rate-path update event, when the energy-CPI gap from deal execution will be fully incorporated. The 30-year yield remains near 5% — not yet reflecting the full deflationary impulse of the supply-shock resolution.

items.headline: CRITICAL: Upriver Fire (Spokane NE) WUI Day 2 — 11,000+ Evacuations, 2,340 Structures, 15+ Homes Destroyed, 1 Missing, ~10% Containment — First WUI Structure-Loss Fire of 2026 Season; Governor Ferguson Requests FEMA Declaration
items.summary: The Upriver Fire — ignited June 17 northeast of Spokane, Washington, near Upriver Drive and Felts Field — escalated sharply into its second day as the defining new infrastructure and humanitarian threat of the June 18 brief. High winds drove the fire into densely populated Spokane County neighborhoods, forcing Level 3 ('GO NOW') evacuations in areas spanning roughly Upriver Drive across from Felts Field Area Park to Bigelow Gulch Road, Thierman Road to Argonne Road, with Level 2 evacuations extending further. More than 11,000 people are under evacuation orders. Approximately 2,340 primary and secondary structures are within the evacuation zone. At least 15 homes have been confirmed burned as of the evening cycle. Approximately 500 additional homes are actively threatened. One person was reported missing by a family member; emergency responders could not access the fire zone to search due to dangerous conditions as of late Tuesday. An emergency shelter opened at Spokane Valley United Methodist Church for displaced residents. Governor Bob Ferguson has formally requested a FEMA fire management assistance declaration from the Federal Emergency Management Agency — the first state-requested federal fire emergency of the 2026 PNW season, placing the Upriver Fire in the highest federal response tier for wildland fire events. The fire is approximately 10% contained as of available reporting. The Upriver Fire is analytically significant on three levels: first, it is the first confirmed WUI (wildland-urban interface) fire with documented structure loss of the 2026 PNW fire season — the precise failure mode NIFC and Washington EMD identified as the primary catastrophic risk in their above-normal season assessment; second, it is burning northeast of Spokane in an area not part of the eastern Washington fire cluster already under management, adding a third simultaneously active high-complexity fire system to the NIFC-FIFA co-response posture; third, it is generating the highest human impact metrics (evacuations, structure loss, missing person) of any single fire event in the 2026 arc to date. Washington DNR is responding along with Spokane County emergency management. FERC large-load grid implications for the Spokane-Inland Empire corridor are a secondary watch item as the fire burns near electrical infrastructure in the Upriver Drive corridor.

items.summary: Five secondary infrastructure threads entering June 18 evening. First: Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters fire containment breakthroughs are the session's most significant positive infrastructure signal. Juniper Dunes (Franklin County, near Juniper Dunes Wilderness, ~10 miles NE of Pasco) advanced from 0% to 20% containment with the fire growing to 13,144 acres — the first containment progress on the fire since its June 13 ignition. The roadless wilderness terrain continues to force reliance on manual hand-tool operations; heavy machinery cannot be deployed in the Wilderness. Nevertheless, the temperature moderation from the heat event's expiration produced measurable progress. Twin Sisters (Highway 730 area, eastern Washington) is 65% contained at 8,262 acres — a dramatic advance from 0% on June 17, with aerial and ground resources executing effective containment operations in the first moderate-weather window of the season. Level 3 evacuations remain in place for Hatch Grade and nearby areas. Both fires' containment figures, confirmed in the June 17-18 operational window, represent the first positive wildfire operational signal of the 2026 PNW season. Second: Lake Sutherland Fire (Olympic Peninsula, Day 2 from June 17 ignition) — no confirmed acreage update or containment percentage is available through the June 18 evening cycle. Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest resources are responding. The absence of escalating reporting from the Olympic Peninsula through the evening cycle is conditionally reassuring but not confirmatory of containment. Third: Multnomah County heat mortality confirmation — the 24-48 hour lag window from the June 16 95-100°F peak has materialized as documented fatalities. Multnomah County is investigating four suspected heat-related deaths: victims span NE Portland, Lents, Gresham, and downtown. One death was witnessed on Monday; three individuals were found on Monday. The first confirmed victim was a 47-year-old man in the 97211 zip code (NE Portland / Alberta Arts District). King County heat mortality monitoring continues — no confirmed King County heat fatalities reported through the evening cycle. Fourth: BPA grid stabilizing — the post-heat-event demand moderation continues; no emergency grid event has been confirmed across the 5-day window since the June 14 heat onset. The hydropower system has successfully absorbed the season's first major demand surge. Fifth: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory advances to approximately 10 days before end-of-June removal — the June 14-18 heat event and fire weather sequence is exactly the type of compound boundary-layer atmospheric stress the station instruments; July forecasts will operate without this data anchor.

items.headline: Oklahoma Hern Wins Senate Primary; Georgia Collins Advances Senate; Georgia Jackson Defeats Trump-Backed Jones for Governor — First Post-Deal Trump-Endorsed Statewide Loss; WPA Day 110 Moot; Vance CoS Luna Day 2; 'We Won' Frame Day 4
items.summary: Three primary domestic threads entering June 18 evening. First: primary election results finalize from June 16 elections. Kevin Hern wins the Oklahoma Republican Senate primary — advancing to face the Democratic nominee in November. In Georgia Senate runoff, Rep. Mike Collins defeats former college football coach Derek Dooley — Collins will face Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in November, setting up what is expected to be one of the most competitive Senate races of the 2026 cycle. The analytically most significant result is the Georgia Republican gubernatorial runoff: Rick Jackson defeats Lt. Gov. Burt Jones — who had been backed by Trump. This is the first confirmed defeat of a Trump-endorsed statewide Republican candidate in the post-deal primary cycle. The Jones loss is analytically distinct from the Iowa Feenstra loss (June 4, Feenstra positioned against Trump's Iran costs) — Jones was not a deal-opposition candidate but a Trump incumbent who lost to a challenger within the Republican coalition. The result introduces the first data point suggesting that 'deal proximity' and Trump endorsement are not uniformly predictive in post-deal primary environments. The 'we won' frame (Day 4) operates as a national messaging environment but does not appear to be eliminating intra-party competition for state-level offices. Second: JD Vance's new Chief of Staff Nick Luna advances to Day 2 — consolidating Vance's independent political infrastructure concurrent with the deal's formal completion. The CoS transition at signing-eve is analytically consistent with Vance building his 2028 platform infrastructure during the period of maximum political capital generated by the deal arc. Third: WPA Day 110, 20th consecutive day past the hard 90-day constitutional deadline — formally rendered moot with the June 19 signing. No enforcement motion scheduled. The constitutional erosion precedent is locked.

items.summary: June 18 delivers the sharpest single-session bifurcation of the 2026 PNW fire season: dramatic containment progress on existing fires offset by the season's first WUI structure-loss event and documented heat fatalities. The Upriver Fire — northeast Spokane, Day 2 — is now the region's primary emergency response priority. High winds drove the fire through suburban Spokane County density: 11,000+ people under evacuation orders, 2,340 structures in the evacuation zone, 15+ homes confirmed burned, 500+ homes threatened, one person missing. Governor Ferguson's FEMA fire management assistance request is the first of the 2026 PNW season. The fire is approximately 10% contained. The NIFC-FIFA co-response posture on Day 11 now includes four simultaneously active Washington fires of significance (Upriver, Juniper Dunes, Twin Sisters, Lake Sutherland) — the most complex concurrent active-fire environment of the 2026 arc, with the Upriver Fire adding a Spokane-area WUI system to the eastern Washington shrub-steppe cluster already under management. The containment breakthroughs on Juniper Dunes (0% → 20%, 13,144 acres) and Twin Sisters (0% → 65%, 8,262 acres) are the first positive operational fire signal of the season and represent a genuine tactical success — the June 17-18 temperature moderation window produced measurable results before the next heat event (or east wind return) can reset conditions. The operational priority shift is now fully toward the Upriver Fire, with Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters progressing to defensive perimeter consolidation. Lake Sutherland (Olympic Peninsula, Day 2) has not generated escalating reports through the evening cycle — conditionally reassuring but not confirmatory of control. Heat mortality: Multnomah County has confirmed 4 suspected heat-related deaths from the June 14-16 event — the 24-48 hour lag window has now produced its documented fatality cluster. No King County heat deaths confirmed through the evening cycle. BPA hydropower demand has stabilized post-heat-event without a confirmed rotating outage across the full 5-day event window — a significant operational success for the grid under drought-year-4 hydropower constraints. Seattle FIFA T-1: US vs Australia (Pride Weekend, Lumen Field, June 19) proceeds tomorrow under expected moderate post-heat-wave temperatures, SEAR-2 operational posture, and the full NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 12 capacity commitment.

items.headline: NIFC Above-Normal Day 18 — Four Active High-Complexity WA Fires; East Cascades Fuel Drying Accelerating; Washington Drought Day 14 (4th Year); El Niño 61%; NSF Newport OR ~10 Days; Longview CSB Day 24 — Acute Vapor Pressure Risk Closed
items.summary: Five secondary PNW environmental threads entering June 18 evening. First: NIFC above-normal Day 18 with Washington now managing four simultaneously active high-complexity fires (Upriver, Juniper Dunes, Twin Sisters, Lake Sutherland) — the most concurrent complex fire load of the 2026 arc. The Upriver Fire's WUI character adds a new type of operational demand to the NIFC-FIFA co-response posture: structure-defense and civilian evacuation support that stretches beyond the shrub-steppe suppression operations managing Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters. East Cascades fuel drying: the June 14-16 heat event added approximately 3-5 additional drying days to east Cascades shrub-steppe fuels, which were already estimated 10-14 days ahead of historical onset schedule. The 12-day T-12 estimate from June 17 is now T-11 from June 18 — east Cascades onset is approaching. Second: Washington drought emergency Day 14 (4th consecutive year, 50% snowpack) — soil moisture deficits remain acute even with heat event expiration; no precipitation relief is projected through June; the fire season risk envelope extends to October 2026 under current NIFC above-normal designation. Oregon 83% drought monitor coverage with 12-county emergency. El Niño probability 61% (super El Niño 1-in-4). Third: Longview CSB Day 24 — the 90,000-gallon hazardous material storage tank's acute vapor pressure risk window closed with the heat event expiration; no incident was confirmed across the peak window. Tank remains structurally compromised; monitoring continues; the next acute risk window would be the next significant heat event (likely T-3 to T-5 weeks under summer progression). Fourth: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory advancing to approximately 10 days before removal — June 19's US vs Australia FIFA match and associated crowd-surge represents the type of high-density summer event where coastal weather forecasting matters most; Newport data is available for tomorrow's event but not the next month's. Fifth: Gray whale washup pace (Oregon 21 YTD, Washington 17 YTD) continues above expected annual pace; NOAA Pacific prey availability monitoring active.

analyst_summary: June 18, 2026 evening closes at Vibe 6 — the first upgrade in the arc since Vibe 5 was established on June 14-15. Lebanon Quiet Day 3 cleared: all three required pre-signing performance tests have been passed in sequence, and the primary deal-collapse scenario (Israeli Lebanon strike triggering Iranian response before Geneva) has been extinguished across the full T-3 to T-1 window. The Geneva formal signing ceremony is T-0 tomorrow; JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner are confirmed attending; Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is the Iranian signatory. WTI has declined for five consecutive sessions to approximately $75 per barrel — the oil market's authoritative verdict that deal completion is fully priced. Shipping companies and insurance underwriters remain in a wait-and-see posture, holding off on unescorted Hormuz transits until the June 19 formal signing activates the MOU's legal architecture; commercial traffic resumption and the 100+ stuck ships' release are the physical deal-confirmation signals to watch tomorrow. The session's PNW development is the sharpest single-day bifurcation of the 2026 fire season. On the positive side: Juniper Dunes (0% → 20%, 13,144 acres) and Twin Sisters (0% → 65%, 8,262 acres) delivered the first containment breakthroughs of the season in the June 17-18 moderation window — a genuine tactical success for NIFC and Washington DNR. On the negative side: the Upriver Fire northeast of Spokane escalated to the season's first WUI structure-loss event — 11,000+ evacuations, 2,340 structures threatened, 15+ homes burned, one missing person, Governor Ferguson's FEMA fire management assistance request submitted. The Upriver Fire is operating precisely in the WUI failure mode NIFC's above-normal season assessment flagged as the primary catastrophic risk scenario. Separately, Multnomah County's 4 suspected heat-related deaths confirm that the June 14-16 heat event's human cost is now documented, not projected. Three primary next-24-hour watch items for June 19 (T-0): Geneva formal signing (the Vibe 7 upgrade trigger — formal signing confirmation + Hormuz physical reopening announcement = full deal execution; any last-minute repudiation, no-show, or signing deferral = most acute deal-risk event remaining); Upriver Fire containment progress (aerial suppression effectiveness on Day 3 is the critical operational question — does the 10% containment hold overnight or does the fire break toward the 500 threatened homes; the missing person search is the immediate humanitarian priority); Seattle FIFA US vs Australia Pride Weekend (NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 12 at Lumen Field under expected moderate temperatures with concurrent Spokane WUI emergency — the co-response posture is now at maximum operational complexity).
watch_items: Geneva signing T-0 (June 19) — Vance, Witkoff, Kushner confirmed; Ghalibaf Iranian signatory; formal ceremony is the primary Vibe 7 upgrade trigger; signing + Hormuz physical reopening announcement = deal execution complete; any last-minute Iranian MOU repudiation, Israeli overnight escalation, or principal no-show = most acute remaining deal-risk event of the 111-day arc; deal probability now >95% but not 100% until ink is dry

Hormuz commercial traffic resumption — June 19 signing is the expected commercial trigger for shipping companies and insurance underwriters to lift wait-and-see posture; first confirmed unescorted tanker transits + Lloyd's rate normalization announcement + the 100+ stuck ships beginning to move = physical deal-confirmation signals distinct from the political signing; watch ship tracking data and insurance market announcements concurrent with ceremony

Upriver Fire Day 3 (Spokane NE) — first confirmed WUI structure-loss fire of 2026 PNW season; 11,000+ evacuations active; 500 homes threatened; 1 person missing (search imminent as fire zone becomes accessible); FEMA fire management assistance declaration expected; overnight aerial suppression and dawn attack are the critical containment window; any further structure loss or casualty confirmation escalates federal response tier

Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters consolidation — Day 2 post-breakthrough; 20% and 65% containment respectively; maintaining and expanding containment percentages through June 19 moderate weather validates the operational success; any reversal on wind return or temperature increase would indicate breakthrough was weather-window-dependent, not structural

Seattle FIFA US vs Australia June 19 Pride Weekend — NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 12 at Lumen Field; concurrent Spokane WUI emergency creates maximum resource demand split; moderate temperatures expected (strong weather improvement from June 15 90°F opener); Pride Weekend attendance adds demographic complexity; co-response Day 12 is the hardest operational day of the FIFA arc to date given simultaneous Upriver Fire federal response

Reconciliation 2.0 floor scheduling — 16 days to July 4; Speaker Johnson needs a floor date announcement this week for a third-week-of-June attempt; Freedom Caucus Iran-war-cost leverage formally extinguished with Lebanon Day 3 and T-0 tomorrow; any Johnson floor date announcement June 18-19 = legislative countdown activated; continued silence = July deadline math compressing dangerously

Georgia Republican primary aftermath — Rick Jackson defeats Trump-backed Burt Jones in gubernatorial runoff; first Trump-endorsed statewide loss in post-deal primary cycle; watch Trump response (endorsement withdrawal reaction? immediate Jackson pivot?) and whether result is read as a deal-frame anomaly or an early indication of post-deal intra-party primary differentiation

WTI/Brent June 19 on signing — $74-78 range = market confirmation of deal pricing; any sustained recovery above $80 = deal-execution discount on commercial traffic delay; physical Hormuz traffic resumption will be more informative than price alone for assessing full deal operationalization

Multnomah County heat mortality follow-up — 4 suspected heat deaths confirmed; medical examiner investigation ongoing; any additional Portland-area or Seattle-area heat fatalities confirmed in the June 18-19 cycle close the heat event's human cost accounting; no additional reported deaths would be consistent with the June 16 expiration of peak heat

Lake Sutherland Fire Day 3 (Olympic Peninsula) — no June 18 acreage or containment data available; Day 3 reporting will indicate whether the June 17 ignition remained manageable or expanded under post-heat-event conditions; Olympic National Park infrastructure and Highway 101 proximity remain secondary structural risk

Missing person Upriver Fire — one person reported missing by family member as of June 17 evening; search operations pending fire-zone accessibility; confirmation of status (located safe, located injured, or confirmed fatality) is the most immediate humanitarian data point of the June 19 cycle

CISA overnight June 18-19 — FIFA co-response Day 12; Shamkhani cyber Day 26; June 19 signing eve is the last window in which IRGC cyber actors could plausibly attempt a last-ditch infrastructure disruption before the MOU's legal architecture activates; any FBI IC3 flash or venue network incident on signing day = maximum operational complexity
